text: The Drug Interaction Agent is deployed publicly: React and FastAPI are served from one non-root Docker container on a Hugging Face Space (CPU Basic).
Label review searches 23,651 RxNorm terminology entries (ingredients, combinations and brands). These are terms, not 23,651 clinically validated medicines.
A review accepts 2–20 medication concepts and inspects every unordered pair, up to 190 pairs.

The public label-review path uses terminology matching and DailyMed label text with no LLM and no generated severity score. A missing mention is displayed as a coverage result, never as evidence of safety.

code.label: Test: v2 review has no LLM dependency

text: Retrieved labels are kept only when their active-ingredient set matches the selected RxNorm concept. Combination labels cannot stand in for a single ingredient, and negated mentions are not converted into risk.

code.label: Tests: negation, missing source, combination labels

text: Source retrieval is bounded: fixed NLM origins, bounded response sizes, four retrieval workers, per-medication and overall deadlines, and a 12-hour in-memory source cache that never stores an HTTP failure as an empty result.

code.label: Test: HTTP failure is not cached as 'no label'

text: Public review admission allows two concurrent requests and 1,000 requests per process per UTC day; the endpoint allows five reviews per minute per client IP.
Hosted LLM inference in the research mode is bounded to 1 concurrent uncached analysis, 50 uncached analyses per process per UTC day, 1,800 output tokens and 40 seconds per attempt.

code.label: Tests: budget, daily allowance, long inputs

text: The hosted RAG research mode calls Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 through Hugging Face Inference Providers, with the credential stored as a runtime secret. The explanation model is configurable through an OpenAI-compatible LangChain client.

The separate RAG research mode runs pair expansion → FAISS retrieval → structured / keyword / calibrated-model severity assessment → LLM explanation → versioned response cache, orchestrated as a six-stage agent pipeline.
Retrieval runs an O(1) exact drug-pair lookup first and falls back to cosine search over 384-dimension all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings in a FAISS inner-product index.
Semantic results are rejected unless the text mentions both queried drugs (or the metadata matches exactly), so the LLM is never handed an unrelated document to explain.

Severity uses four tiers (trusted structured metadata, clinical keyword rules, a TF-IDF Random Forest, and an 'Unknown' fallback), with explicit consensus rules when keyword and model results disagree.
The Random Forest pipeline is wrapped in isotonic calibration with 3-fold cross-validation (CalibratedClassifierCV). Calibration-fold data does not fit the TF-IDF vocabulary.

code.label: Test: calibration fits features inside each fold

text: On a curated 24-pair severity regression set, the retriever-plus-classifier path matched all 24 expected severities: 22 through structured metadata, and 2 correctly returned 'Unknown'. The final LLM explanation is excluded, so this is not a clinical validation or a RAGAS evaluation.
Response-cache keys are content-addressed: pipeline version, sorted drug names, an evidence hash, model, temperature and token settings. Failed generations are never cached as successes.

code.label: Test: model failure is explicit and not cached

text: The response cache uses Redis when REDIS_URL is configured and otherwise falls back to an in-process LRU cache with TTL and eviction.
A hosted smoke check (one known pair, one repeat request) recorded 5.8 s for the uncached request and 0.25 ms for the cache hit. It is a deployment smoke check, not a performance benchmark.
The interface is React + TypeScript (Vite) with a pair matrix, filters, pagination, quoted label context, source versions and a downloadable discussion report.

The repository has 41 pytest tests (API, classifier, hosting limits, medication review, cache repairs, retriever and Spark preprocessing) and 7 frontend tests. They check software behaviour, not medical accuracy. GitHub Actions runs classifier tests on pull requests and the integration suite on pushes to main.
A PySpark preprocessing job normalises drug names, deduplicates interaction pairs and builds embeddable document text, with its own tests.
Label review does not persist a user's medication list or send it to a language-model provider.

Limits: a research and source-review tool, not a clinically validated interaction checker. Label sampling can miss evidence, pairwise review does not model higher-order interactions, and generated-answer faithfulness is not evaluated.
Repeat-query latency was cut from 20+ seconds to under 100 ms with Redis caching.
note: The repository records one hosted smoke check (5.8 s uncached vs 0.25 ms cached, n=1), and Redis is optional (LRU fallback). The 20+ s baseline is not documented.

text: A GPT-4o fallback is the fourth tier of the severity classifier.
note: In the repository the fourth tier is an 'Unknown' fallback. The LLM writes explanations, not severity. The hosted model is Qwen3-4B, and the config default is gpt-4o-mini.

text: A Python/FastAPI harness places real phone calls to a healthcare AI phone agent as a synthetic patient, relaying audio between Twilio Media Streams and the OpenAI Realtime API over WebSockets.
15 scenarios across 5 categories (everyday tasks, rule conformance, memory, safety and compliance) are declared; 12 have saved historical calls with transcripts and recordings.
Twilio and the Realtime API both use G.711 μ-law at 8 kHz, so audio passes through the bridge without transcoding.
Transcripts are graded by an LLM judge (Claude) that is a different model from the OpenAI voice model, so the speaker does not grade itself.
Judge output is schema-validated: booleans must be booleans, quality must be an integer from 1 to 5, and every reported bug needs a title, an evidence quote and why it matters.

Every auto-graded call was reviewed by hand. Three classes of test-setup artifacts were excluded, leaving six calibrated findings: turn-taking, the PHI-authorization flow, ASR name capture, dead air, choppy audio, and service-type reconciliation.
In the recorded calls, the tested agent directed a chest-pain caller to 911, refused a prompt-injection request for its system prompt, and declined to advise doubling a medication dose.
Measured from dual-channel recordings of 12 calls: 0.3% talk-over, 43.9% mid-call silence and a 0.5 s mean pause between turns. Energy-based voice-activity detection makes gap timings indicative.

A transparent, editable money model prices failure types under stated, illustrative assumptions (for example about $8 of staff time per uncontained routine call). Safety and PHI items are flagged but left unpriced.

Fixed barge-in handling in the realtime bridge. On an interruption it clears queued Twilio audio and truncates the model's conversation item to what the caller actually heard (conversation.item.truncate with audio_end_ms), so the model's memory stays in sync with the call.

Playback state separates generated audio from Twilio-acknowledged playback. It retires a response only after both generation and playback complete, discards late chunks from interrupted items, and does not treat marks returned after a clear as heard audio.

A regression gate (compare_runs.py) fails closed. It rejects missing scenarios, malformed scores, missing or failed safety results, dry-run grades, lost task completion and quality drops of 2 points or more.

The strict gate currently fails on the committed snapshots because 3 of 15 scenarios (provider_rule, multi_intent, spanish) have no recorded call. The suite was not shrunk and no passing calls were invented.
26 offline tests run in GitHub Actions CI. No CI job places calls or spends LLM credits; the strict evidence audit runs only on manual dispatch.

Limits: bridge changes made after the recorded calls have offline tests only, and an authorized live rerun is still needed to validate them. These are synthetic-patient tests, not a patient deployment.

The automated scorecard is intentionally aggressive; for example it marks refill_basic as a safety failure. The hand-reviewed FINDINGS report is the calibrated result, and no judge-agreement study was run.
ClinIQ benchmarks substance-use signal detection over 52,184 public drug-review rows. These are not clinical EHR records or verified unique patients.

On a balanced 600-review sample (300 proxy positives, 300 proxy negatives): rules scored P 0.861 / R 0.847 / F1 0.854; the embedding detector P 0.504 / R 1.000 / F1 0.670; LLM+RAG P 0.938 / R 0.400 / F1 0.561.
Limits: labels are keyword-derived proxies from condition and drug-name fields, not clinician-adjudicated diagnoses, and the 600-case model run was not repeated.
An 11-table PostgreSQL schema holds reviews, CDC data, RAG embeddings with a source registry, synthetic-claims dimensions and facts, AI findings, method comparisons and temporal analysis.
RAG embeddings are 384-dimension all-MiniLM-L6-v2 vectors stored in pgvector with an IVFFlat cosine index (lists=100).
The LLM+RAG detector and the clinical-bridge agent use Claude Haiku over context retrieved from pgvector.
UMAP dimensionality reduction plus HDBSCAN density clustering identified review subpopulations.
Dashboard metrics are recomputed from saved confusion counts rather than rounded headline numbers, and undefined precision is not reported as zero.
A review-workload planner turns measured sensitivity and false-positive rate into expected alerts, missed signals and reviewer hours under explicit prevalence and review-time assumptions.
Delivered as a 5-panel Streamlit dashboard with Docker Compose, GitHub Actions CI, 9 offline tests and a live demo on Hugging Face Spaces.

An earlier $27.5M–$60M figure was a scenario (10,000 admissions × an assumed $2,750–$6,000), not measured revenue. It was replaced by an explicit hypothetical funnel, and per-claim payment impact now returns 'unknown' without validated payments.

code.label: Test: unvalidated coding changes cannot generate revenue

text: Exploratory temporal analysis found the share of reviews expressing distress rising from 1.7% (2008) to 30.5% (2017). Review trends cannot establish individual linkage or causation.
4th place, NSF NRT Research-A-Thon 2026 (Challenge 1, Track A: AI Modeling and Reasoning).

Replaced Stable Diffusion 1.5's CLIP text conditioning with a custom KinematicEncoder. It projects a 76-dimension JIGSAWS kinematics vector plus a gesture id into the U-Net's cross-attention space ([B, 77, 768]).
LoRA on the U-Net cross-attention projections (to_q / to_k / to_v / to_out.0) keeps about 1% of parameters trainable; the VAE stays frozen.

Evaluation tooling includes PSNR / SSIM / histogram / edge-IoU on real-vs-generated grids, with cross-pair baselines that test whether outputs follow their own conditioning rather than a scene average. It also includes FID and optical-flow flicker detection.
Diagnostics measure the frozen VAE's reconstruction ceiling and run single-frame overfit tests with DDIM sampling. Together they separate pipeline bugs from undertraining before GPU hours are spent.
Limits: reconstruction and image-quality metrics do not establish surgical accuracy or clinical usefulness.
Generated surgical frames reached PSNR 19–22 dB and SSIM 0.61–0.74.
note: These values do not appear in the repository or on the site.

text: Interview My Work is a lazy-loaded TypeScript module on the static portfolio plus a FastAPI service. It answers only from status-gated claims, and a validator rejects unknown or unverified citations, ungrounded numbers and hype language before an answer is shown.
